summary_en: Third-party committee investigation into December 2025 excess buyback (above distributable amount under Companies Act) completed. Board adopted remediation: revised authority matrix and rules of business division; employee and board training on distributable amount rules and related laws; strengthened compliance framework with enhanced board-paper standards and external advisor engagement.
title_en: Remediation Measures Based on Third-Party Committee Investigation Report Regarding Self-Share Acquisition Exceeding Distributable Amount
translation_en_brief:
On 17 July 2026, Senko Group Holdings disclosed a board-approved remediation framework following a third-party committee investigation into an excess share buyback executed on 5 December 2025. The company had acquired treasury shares in excess of the distributable amount calculated under the Companies Act and Companies Accounting Regulations. No financial statement or earnings forecast impact is expected.

The third-party committee recommended three categories of remediation. First, establish effective distributable-amount governance: codify the responsible departments, role allocations, workflow, and approval checkpoints; institute multi-person verification of distributable-amount calculations with audit-committee reporting; and ensure cross-functional coordination and information sharing. Second, deliver training to relevant staff and officers on distributable-amount mechanics and complex securities/corporate law. Third, strengthen compliance: maintain documented audit trails visible to the board and audit committee, analyse dividend and buyback decisions against consolidated and standalone performance using long-term projections, and engage external counsel and auditors proactively.

The board resolved to revise the authority matrix to specify decision rights and approval routes for surplus allocation and dividend/buyback decisions; amend the business-division rules to identify the responsible departments; prepare a process manual for distributable-amount calculation and distribution policy; conduct employee training on distributable-amount regulation and methodology; hold board-level training led by external counsel on key compliance rules; and formalize board-paper standards requiring detailed distributable-amount calculation bases, external-counsel consultation summaries, and inter-department pre-review and sign-off.
